proseChanges.summary: **Notification recipients and bulk reads at scale:** notification recipients are read by contact id through two seekable arms, for the conversation contact and its participants, instead of walking every contact in a large imported workspace. Bulk preparation and version refresh also seek conversations by id. Recipient columns, aliases, workspace checks and results are unchanged. No migration. **Fixes — Mailgun webhook signing key declaration:** the packaging recipe and the emitted deployment spec now declare `MAILGUN_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_KEY` as an optional secret, as `scripts/deployment/environment.mjs` already did, so the platform's release check no longer reports a secret-name mismatch. Installs without Mailgun are unaffected, and the build and `verify:build` now fail when packaging omits any runtime secret name. No migration. **Legacy import fidelity:** a full legacy import no longer leaves trigger-written rows in the integration-event and workflow journals (so `check.mjs work` counts, now including `workflow_events`, stay unchanged) and leaves each imported workspace's default "Close solved tickets after 4 days" rule a draft instead of published (`--publish-default-rules` keeps it published); legacy messages with no author import as role `system` instead of an operator reply, with `message_authorship` written where the kind is known; and imported conversations open read for the workspace's members (`--leave-unread` keeps them unread). Documented in docs/LEGACY-EXPORT.md. **Sign out under load:** `/auth/*` (sign out, bootstrap, owner claim) is reserved from the public site, so a busy database no longer makes a sign out wait on, or fail at, the Help Center alias lookup before the application answers it. A Help Center alias can no longer be named `auth`. **Erasure follow-ups:** an erased person's files no longer outlive a stalled legacy import (an import whose lease lapsed keeps no file it uploaded, and an erased contact's leftover files are removed on the next run); a full legacy package import respects erasures as a delta does and imports nothing of an erased contact; an import keeps another customer's shared file in every order; an erasure request that waited for a running erasure of the same contact answers the completed record, while any other repeat erases what arrived since; and a contact whose erasure failed shows it as pending on its page, with the erase action to complete it. This change adds no migration. **Legacy import repair:** an installation whose full legacy import ran before the fidelity round keeps the trigger-written rows that import left (`native_integration_events` `contact.created`, `conversation.status_changed` and `article.published`, and `workflow_events`, which `check.mjs work` counts). Migration 320 removes exactly those: it reads the import's own journal (`legacy_import_rows`, `legacy_import_runs`) for the contacts, conversations and articles a full import wrote and deletes only the events of those entities stamped inside that import's run window, plus the waiting-visitor rows only the import's own visitor authorship derived (the delete re-derives the inbox entry's flags). Whatever a member or customer did afterwards, an event an integration intent already names, a delta sweep's rows and any package with an unfinished run stay. It touches no workflow rule: the default "Close solved tickets after 4 days" rule stays as the workspace has it, and the scheduler never acts on imported conversations either way. Idempotent; an installation that never imported is untouched. See docs/LEGACY-EXPORT.md.

proseChanges.ownerAction: Update from v0.4.16 without resetting. Back up D1, R2, Durable Object state and private settings first. Use Node 22.20.0, pnpm 10.12.4 and pinned rer 0.2.105. Retain native owners, permissions, support history, files, erasure fences and every applied migration identity. Apply the missing migrations once, in filename order, BEFORE the new Worker serves traffic: 320_legacy_import_work_repair.sql. Earlier installations, including v0.4.13, also apply every intervening missing published migration in order; retain each migration's buyer steps. Run `rer deploy --dry-run` against the retained installation before any separately authorized deployment. No reset, cutover or production deployment is part of this release. Live-provider qualification and owner cutover remain separate.
